source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: A Mechanism-Level Review
finding: The review maps 10 historical architectures to modern agent systems, one mechanism at a time. It codes evidence relation (E1-E4) apart from migration depth (D0-D4).
numbers: 10 architectures, 8 runtime families, 42 mechanism-focused systems; 28 pages. E1 = source cites lineage, E2 = implemented structure, E3 = comparable control with different build, E4 = convergence without transfer.
quote: independent convergence rather than documented inheritance
limits: Review only. It states it makes no PRISMA completeness claim and no causal performance claim. Single version, not peer reviewed.
agent_relevance: Treat its map as a design checklist, not as proof that any mechanism helps.

source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: A Mechanism-Level Review
finding: Four equivalence tests stop shallow mappings: a message bus is not a global workspace, a checkpoint is not a Soar impasse substate, a handoff is not BDI commitment, a guardrail is not MIDCA diagnosis.
numbers: 4 tests; D3 = trigger runs the control step by itself; D4 = outcome updates future control policy.
limits: Tests are the authors' own coding rules; no inter-rater agreement found in the text read.
agent_relevance: Our schema's operators should pass these tests, else they are only labels.

source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: A Mechanism-Level Review
finding: Six candidate gaps came out of the ledger. Closest-baseline screening closed one (skill governance, B5) because GraSP already has calibrated skill choice, node verification, bounded repair and replanning/ReAct fallback (E3/D4). Five stay open.
numbers: 6 candidates -> 5 residual bundles: activation+latency+utility; typed impasse with isolated substate and resolution compilation; bounded content competition; persistent intention with reconsideration; uncertainty with resource allocation and stopping.
limits: Gaps are conditional on the frozen corpus. Residual means not found composed in the reviewed systems, not shown to matter.
agent_relevance: Cheap list of what our scaffold lacks versus Soar/ACT-R. Impasse-typed recovery and stop rules map to our guardrails.

source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: A Mechanism-Level Review
finding: ACT-R side: adaptive memory systems (AgeMem, Memory-R1, MemCon) reach E3/D4 by learning memory operations from outcomes, but none couples activation, retrieval latency and action utility in one law.
numbers: Rated E3/D4 for memory; coupling rated residual.
limits: Rating is by the authors; the cited systems were not rerun.
agent_relevance: A memory policy should use one score for recency, use value and cost, not separate hacks.

source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: A Mechanism-Level Review
finding: Soar side: PALADIN, AgentDebugX, Shepherd, Reflexion and AgentHER give failure typing, rerun and reversible branches (E2/D3), but none couples a typed impasse to an isolated child state, a typed return and chunking of only the supporting conditions.
numbers: Rated E2/D3 for failure control; B2 residual.
limits: Absence claim is within the corpus only.
agent_relevance: Our impasse-to-subgoal operator has least modern precedent, so it needs its own test.

source: Fan & Lan (2026) From Cognitive Architectures to Language Agents: A Mechanism-Level Review
finding: The paper proposes a durable state x=(intention, workspace, memory, skills, uncertainty, budget, failure substate) where the LLM only proposes and an external governor picks the transition.
numbers: x_t=(i,w,m,s,u,b,q); p_t=LLM(w,i,q); a_t=G(x_t,p_t).
limits: A formalism, not tested. It says current runtimes leave G implicit in code or hand it to another model call.
agent_relevance: Matches our scaffold idea: model proposes, scaffold decides. Keep the governor outside the model.

source: Sumers, Yao, Narasimhan, Griffiths (2023) Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents (CoALA)
finding: CoALA frames an LLM as a production system over strings. It adds modular memory, a structured action space (internal: retrieve, reason, learn; external: grounding) and a decision cycle of planning then execution.
numbers: Survey framework; no benchmark numbers.
quote: just as productions indicate possible ways to modify strings, LLMs define a distribution over changes or additions to text
limits: Taxonomy only. It does not test whether any CoALA component raises performance.
agent_relevance: Common vocabulary; the 2026 review builds on it. Our S-states and O-operators can be mapped to it.

source: Sumers, Yao, Narasimhan, Griffiths (2023) Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents (CoALA)
finding: CoALA notes that LLMs are stateless across calls, so all memory must be written outside the model.
numbers: Qualitative.
quote: Language models are stateless: they do not persist information across calls.
limits: Design observation, not experiment.
agent_relevance: Every persisted state in our scaffold is a design decision; none comes for free.

source: Yao et al. (2022) ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
finding: On ALFWorld (PaLM-540B, 6 controlled trials), best ReAct reached 71% success, best Act-only 45%, best BUTLER (trained) 37%. Even the worst ReAct trial (48%) beat the best Act trial.
numbers: Relative gain of ReAct over Act 33%-90%, mean 62%, over six trials. Abstract: +34% abs. ALFWorld, +10% abs. WebShop over imitation/RL.
limits: Few-shot prompts; one model family; synthetic text game.
agent_relevance: Thought-then-act is the lightest working-memory/decision cycle; keep a thought step before each action.

source: Yao et al. (2022) ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
finding: On HotpotQA and Fever, ReAct alone did not beat chain-of-thought on HotpotQA; combining ReAct with CoT-SC did best.
numbers: HotpotQA EM / Fever acc: Standard 28.7/57.1; CoT 29.4/56.3; CoT-SC 33.4/60.4; Act 25.7/58.9; ReAct 27.4/60.9; CoT-SC->ReAct 34.2/64.6; ReAct->CoT-SC 35.1/62.0.
limits: PaLM-540B only; table read from PDF text, column order checked against row labels.
agent_relevance: Acting is not always better than thinking; use a fallback between modes (a Soar-style method switch).

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Reflexion stores verbal self-reflections in an episodic buffer (last 3 kept). On ALFWorld, ReAct+Reflexion completed 130 of 134 tasks over 12 trials; ReAct alone stopped improving between trial 6 and 7.
numbers: 130/134 tasks; abstract: +22% ALFWorld, +20% HotPotQA, +11% HumanEval over baselines.
limits: Needs a success signal or heuristic to trigger reflection; the HotPotQA setup used ground-truth correctness as a signal.
agent_relevance: Reflection is the episodic-memory plus learning loop of a cognitive architecture; it works when the signal is external.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: HumanEval Python pass@1 rose to 91.0 vs 80.1 for GPT-4 alone. But on Leetcode Hard Python Reflexion scored 77.1 vs 80.1 for GPT-4, a loss.
numbers: HumanEval 91.0 vs 80.1; Leetcode Hard (PY) 77.1 vs 80.1.
limits: Reflexion used self-generated unit tests, a weak external signal; the paper notes a false-positive risk.
agent_relevance: Mixed result at a boundary: gains depend on the quality of the feedback source.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: With oracle labels, self-correction looked strong; with intrinsic correction (no labels) it did not help or made things worse. This challenges how Reflexion-type gains are measured.
numbers: GPT-3.5 oracle: GSM8K 75.9->95.5, HotpotQA 26.0->49.0. Intrinsic GPT-3.5: GSM8K 75.9->75.1->74.7; CommonSenseQA 75.8->38.1->41.8; HotpotQA 26.0->25.0. GPT-4 intrinsic: GSM8K 95.5->91.5->89.0; HotpotQA 49.0->49.0->43.0.
quote: The fundamental issue is that LLMs cannot properly judge the correctness of their reasoning.
limits: Oracle-table rows are garbled in the PDF text, so only GSM8K and HotpotQA oracle cells are quoted. 100 HotpotQA examples; GPT-3.5/GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: Our guardrails should not rely on the model to check its own answer; use an external check.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: For GSM8K, GPT-3.5 kept its first answer 74.7% of the time over two rounds. Of the changes, correct-to-wrong happened more often than wrong-to-correct.
numbers: 74.7% unchanged (GSM8K, GPT-3.5).
limits: One model; prompts from source papers with format additions.
agent_relevance: A self-critique step can lower accuracy; test it before adding it.

source: Kamoi et al. (2024) When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey
finding: Survey: no prior work shows successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs, except on tasks exceptionally suited to it. It works with reliable external feedback and after large-scale fine-tuning.
numbers: Three findings in abstract; many studies use oracle info or weak initial prompts.
quote: no prior work demonstrates successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs
limits: Covers work to early 2024; later reasoning models not covered.
agent_relevance: Supports external verifiers in a scaffold and doubts in-context reflection alone.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
finding: An architecture with memory stream (recency, importance, relevance retrieval), reflection and planning was ablated. 100 raters ranked five conditions on believability; the full architecture ranked best and each removal lowered the score.
numbers: TrueSkill mu: full 29.89; no reflection 26.88; no reflection or planning 25.64; crowdworker 22.95; no memory/planning/reflection 21.21. Full vs prior-work condition d = 8.16. Kruskal-Wallis chi2(4)=150.29, p<0.001; all Dunn pairs significant except crowdworker vs fully ablated.
limits: Believability is rater judgment, not task success. Short 2-day simulation.
agent_relevance: Retrieval scoring like ACT-R base-level activation plus reflection helps believability. It is not evidence of better reasoning.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with LLMs
finding: Voyager combines an automatic curriculum, a skill library and iterative prompting with self-verification. It got 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer travel, and unlocked wooden/stone/iron 15.3x/8.5x/6.4x faster than baselines; only it reached diamond.
numbers: 3.3x items, 2.3x distance, 15.3x/8.5x/6.4x faster tech-tree levels, 160 prompt iterations.
limits: Baselines (ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT) were re-interpreted for Minecraft; GPT-4 only; few runs.
agent_relevance: Skill library = procedural memory, the target of Soar chunking too.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with LLMs
finding: Ablations: random curriculum cut discovered items 93%; removing self-verification cut them 73% (the most important feedback type); GPT-3.5 for code gave 5.7x fewer items than GPT-4; no skill library plateaued late.
numbers: -93% (random curriculum), -73% (no self-verification), GPT-4 gives 5.7x more unique items than GPT-3.5.
quote: Self-verification is the most important among all the feedback types.
limits: Self-verification checks environment state (inventory), an external signal unlike pure self-critique.
agent_relevance: Copy two parts: goal ordering and a verifier tied to observed state.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
finding: Tiered memory, with the model paging items in and out of context, raised deep-memory-retrieval accuracy a lot on a multi-session chat task.
numbers: DMR accuracy: GPT-3.5 38.7% -> 66.9%; GPT-4 32.1% -> 92.5%; GPT-4 Turbo 35.3% -> 93.4% with MemGPT.
limits: Self-built benchmark; baseline is fixed-context truncation.
agent_relevance: Working versus long-term memory split gives large gains when context is the bottleneck.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs
finding: Search over thoughts with an LLM value step solved far more Game of 24 than chain-of-thought.
numbers: GPT-4 Game of 24: IO 7.3%, CoT-SC (k=100) 9.0%, ToT b=1 45%, ToT b=5 74%, CoT about 4%.
limits: Bounded puzzle; many more calls; states are checkable here.
agent_relevance: Subgoal search with evaluation fits Soar's operator-selection space; gains come from search, not wording.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Language Agent Tree Search (LATS)
finding: LATS adds Monte Carlo tree search with environment feedback and reflection on top of ReAct. It reports 92.7% pass@1 on HumanEval with GPT-4 and 75.9 average on WebShop with GPT-3.5.
numbers: 92.7 pass@1 HumanEval (GPT-4); 75.9 WebShop average score (GPT-3.5).
limits: Higher compute per task; HumanEval near saturation.
agent_relevance: Search plus external feedback beats single-path agents, at a cost.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2023) On the Planning Abilities of LLMs
finding: Plain LLMs rarely generate executable plans on IPC-style domains, while humans in a pilot did well. This is a baseline for why a planner or verifier sits outside the model.
numbers: About 3% of generated plans executable; human blocksworld baseline 39 of 50 valid (78%), 35 optimal (89.7% of those).
quote: Only about 3% of the plans that LLMs generate are actually executable
limits: Old models (GPT-3 family, BLOOM); newer reasoning models score far higher.
agent_relevance: Use external plan validation, as Soar uses explicit problem spaces and operators.

source: Kirk, Wray, Lindes, Laird (2024) Improving Knowledge Extraction from LLMs for Robotic Task Learning through Agent Analysis (STARS)
finding: A Soar-based agent uses an LLM as a knowledge source, with analysis and repair of responses and optional human oversight. STARS beat template-based prompting without oversight.
numbers: Completion without oversight 77.5% (tidy kitchen), 94.4% (store groceries), 92.9% (organize office) vs template prompting 52.5%, 66.7%, 35.7%; with oversight 100%. Over 70% of raw LLM responses not viable in one task.
limits: Three tasks, simulated robot; one model family.
agent_relevance: Direct support for the Soar pattern: LLM proposes, the agent analyses and repairs, then a check or person accepts.

source: Wray, Kirk, Laird (2025) Applying Cognitive Design Patterns to General LLM Agents
finding: Argues agentic LLM systems have independently re-found Soar and ACT-R patterns (buffers, operator proposal and selection, episodic and semantic memory) and names step-wise reflection as a new pattern.
numbers: Table 1 of patterns; no benchmark numbers.
limits: Position paper by Soar developers; no experiments.
agent_relevance: Same convergence claim as the 2026 review, from the architecture builders. Good for naming, not proof.

source: Wray, Kirk, Laird (2024) Eliciting Problem Specifications via LLMs
finding: An LLM task-analyst agent writes problem-space specs (states, operators, goals, search control) that a cognitive system solves by weak methods. Specs that list operators but omit search control cost orders of magnitude more steps.
numbers: Qualitative; preliminary results.
limits: Authors call it preliminary; few problem classes.
agent_relevance: Search control is the weak spot; a scaffold needs it explicit.

source: NL2GenSym (2025) Natural Language to Generative Symbolic Rules for SOAR via LLMs
finding: An LLM generator plus execution-grounded critic writes Soar rules. Success rate beats one-shot prompting, and a small model with the framework beat a larger model with one-shot.
numbers: Gemini-2.5-Pro: manual 84%, one-shot 55%, NL2GenSym 86%; qwen-max one-shot 66% vs 91%; Flash+framework 86% beats Pro one-shot 55%; zero-shot 0%.
limits: Own benchmark; one author group.
agent_relevance: Execution-grounded critique is the key part, in line with the self-correction literature.

source: NL2GenSym (2025) Natural Language to Generative Symbolic Rules for SOAR via LLMs
finding: Ablation of the same framework: removing the critic cost the most.
numbers: Critic removed: success rate -23% overall, -37% on hard and variable cases; basic knowledge base removed -17%; case knowledge base removed -14%.
limits: Same limits as above.
agent_relevance: Feedback from a real execution is worth more than extra stored knowledge.
